prerequisites.why: The b = 2 and b = 3 cases of Theorem 1.2 and the template for the whole argument: the definition of rapid decay (Definition 5.1.1), the proof of the decay lemma in the b ≤ 3 case (Theorem 5.1.2 and Proposition 5.1.3), the global–local comparison (Definition 7.1.3, Remark 7.2.2, Corollary 7.2.4, Lemma 8.2.2) and the Siegel mass formula in this setting (Theorem 4.2.2). The present paper repeatedly reduces to computations carried out there.

prerequisites.citation: Stephen Kudla and Michael Rapoport, "Special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties II: Global theory", J. Reine Angew. Math. 697 (2014), 91–157; and Bruinier–Howard–Kudla–Rapoport–Yang, "Modularity of generating series of divisors on unitary Shimura varieties"
prerequisites.why: The unitary Shimura variety of signature (n,1) with its integral model, special divisors and arithmetic compactifications, which is what Remark 8.12 needs for the unitary half of Theorem 1.4.

prerequisites.citation: Peter Sarnak, "Some applications of modular forms", Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics 99, Cambridge University Press (1990)
prerequisites.why: The trivial bound on the Fourier coefficients of a cusp form of weight k (Proposition 1.3.5), which is the error term in Lemma 7.5 and in the theta-series decomposition of §7.14.

prerequisites.citation: Keiji Oguiso, "Local families of K3 surfaces and applications", J. Algebraic Geom. 12 (2003), 405–433; and Claire Voisin, Théorie de Hodge et géométrie algébrique complexe, SMF (2002)
prerequisites.why: The characteristic-zero statement, due to Green, that the Noether–Lefschetz locus of a non-isotrivial family of K3 surfaces over a disc is countable and dense. Theorem 1.1 is its characteristic-p analogue, and a roadmap planning Theorem 1.1 should carry it as the comparison statement.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: orthogonal integral models, Kuga–Satake and special divisors
routes.brief: This reuses the candidate id already proposed by PAPER-CHARLES-16, PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 and PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22, and adds to it what this paper needs. Those briefs build the orthogonal integral model of a GSpin Shimura variety, the Kuga-Satake abelian scheme with its C(L)-action, the realisations of 𝐋 and the special divisors 𝒵(m); the items added here are the same objects in the case this paper works in, namely (L,Q) of signature (b,2) self-dual at p with hyperspecial level, together with what the special fibre needs. Construct: the datum (G_Q, D_L) with G = GSpin(L ⊗ Z_(p)) and reflex field Q, the level 𝕂 with 𝕂_p = G(Z_p), and Kisin's canonical smooth integral model 𝒮 over Z_(p); the Kuga-Satake abelian scheme 𝒜^univ → 𝒮 with its C(L)-action and the cohomologies 𝐇_B, 𝐇_dR, 𝐇_{ℓ,ét} and 𝐇_cris; the local systems 𝐋_B, 𝐋_dR, 𝐋_{ℓ,ét} and the F-crystal 𝐋_cris inside End_{C(L)}(𝐇_?), compatible under the comparison isomorphisms, with the quadratic form 𝐐 defined by f ∘ f = 𝐐(f)Id; special endomorphisms of 𝒜^univ_T and of 𝒜^univ_T[p^∞]; the special divisor 𝒵(m) as a Deligne-Mumford stack over 𝒮, an effective Cartier divisor flat over Z_(p), with Z(m) its special fibre; the tautological line bundle ω attached to Fil^1 V and the Hasse invariant as a section of ω^{p-1}; and, for the boundary, the fact that the cusps of 𝒮^BB are 0- or 1-dimensional, with a 1-dimensional cusp given by a saturated isotropic rank-2 sublattice I ⊂ L and Λ = I^⊥/I. The final statements are: Remark 2.4, that an endomorphism is special as soon as it is special at one geometric point, and that over an 𝒮_{F_p}-scheme only the crystalline realisation has to be checked; Remark 2.5, that v ∘ v = [Q(v)] with Q positive definite on the lattice of special endomorphisms; Definition 2.6 with the flatness and effective-Cartier property of 𝒵(m); the identity i_P(C.Z(m)) = Σ_{n≥1} #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m} for a curve lying in no special divisor, where L_n is the lattice of special endomorphisms of the pullback of 𝒜^univ modulo t^n, together with ∩_n L_n = 0 and the constancy of the rank; the dichotomy rk_Z L_1 = b+2 if and only if P is supersingular, and rk_Z L_1 ≤ b otherwise; and the description, up to a finite quotient, of π^{-1}(Υ) over a 1-dimensional cusp Υ as a torsor under ℰ ⊗_Z Λ over a modular curve. Import Shimura data from ShimuraData D2, the analytic tower and the Hodge type from ShimuraVarieties V1 and V6, Baily-Borel algebraicity from V2, abelian schemes and their deformation theory from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, Dieudonné theory from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2, crystals from CrystallineCohomology CR.1 and CR.3, the modular curve and its universal elliptic curve from the Tau Ceti modular-curves roadmap, and Clifford algebras with the spin group from Mathlib. Do not plan the characteristic-p decay theory or the Hecke orbit argument here: they are the separate new roadmap SupersingularCrystalsAndOrdinaryHeckeOrbits proposed by this extraction.
routes.reason: Every item on this route is part of the standing set-up that the number-field companion paper PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 already routed here, in the same words: the GSpin integral model, the Kuga-Satake scheme, the realisations of 𝐋, special endomorphisms, the special divisors, the identity of its Lemma 7.2 and the supersingular rank statement of its Proposition 7.3. Keeping them together in one Part II is what PROTOCOL section 15 asks for, and splitting them off from the characteristic-p engine is what keeps the new roadmap honest about what it adds. ShimuraVarieties itself stops at generic-fibre canonical models and ShimuraData's examples do not include the GSpin datum, so these are not planned anywhere in the atlas. The two items the earlier briefs do not mention, the Hasse invariant as a section of ω^{p-1} and the orthogonal cusp geometry, belong here rather than in the new roadmap because they are statements about the model and its compactification, not about supersingular crystals.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: heights of GSpin special divisors and exceptional reductions
routes.brief: This reuses the candidate id proposed by PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 and PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22, whose briefs already construct ρ_L and M_{1+b/2}(ρ_L), the Eisenstein series E_0 with constant term 2𝔢_0, the Bruinier-Kuss coefficients c(β,m) with |c(m)| ≍ m^{b/2}, and the Howard-Madapusi Pera modularity theorem in its arithmetic form. The items added here are the three of those statements that this paper uses, in the geometric normalisation it uses them in, so that the same lane owns them once. Construct: the dual lattice L^∨, the basis {𝔢_μ} of C[L^∨/L], the Weil representation ρ_L of Mp_2(Z) on it, and the Eisenstein series E_0(τ) = Σ_{Γ'_∞\Mp_2(Z)} σ(τ)^{-(2+n)}ρ_L(g,σ)^{-1}𝔢_0 of weight 1 + b/2, with constant term 𝔢_0 and Fourier coefficients q_L(m). The final statements are: the Bruinier-Kuss formulae for q_L(m) in the even and the odd case, in terms of σ_{-b/2}(m,χ), √|L^∨/L|, Γ(1+b/2), Dirichlet L-values, ζ(b+1) and the local densities δ(ℓ,L,m), together with the consequence |q_L(m)| ≍ m^{b/2} for every m represented by (L,Q); and the modularity statement that -(ω.C) + Σ_m Z(m).C is the 𝔢_0-component of a modular form of weight 1 + b/2 for ρ_L with Eisenstein part -(ω.C)E_0, whence Z(m).C = |q_L(m)|(ω.C) + O(m^{(b+2)/4}) and Σ_{m ∈ S_X} Z(m).C ≍ X^{1+b/2}. The error term is the trivial bound on the coefficients of a cusp form of weight 1 + b/2, so that bound is part of what this lane must supply. Import the metaplectic cover and the general Weil representation from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.1 and MP.4, the special divisors and ω from OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake, local densities from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3, and Dirichlet L-functions from AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1.
routes.reason: The three items are the global input of this paper's argument, and they are the same three objects that the sibling extraction of Shankar-Shankar-Tang-Tayou already routed to this Part II: ρ_L with E_0, the Bruinier-Kuss coefficients, and the modularity of the generating series of special divisors. They do not belong in the new characteristic-p roadmap, which consumes them; nor in OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake, which owns the model and the divisors but not the automorphic generating series. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.6 plans modularity of Chow-valued generating series only on Shimura curves.

routes.title: Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type
routes.brief: This reuses the candidate id proposed by PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24, whose brief constructs, for a Hodge-type datum with hyperspecial level at p and neat prime-to-p level, the integral mixed Shimura data at each cusp, the abelian scheme and torus torsor over it, the integral torus embeddings for smooth admissible fans, and the formal-completion comparison with the integral toroidal compactification, all following Madapusi Pera. The items added here are the three statements of that theory that the Hecke-orbit argument of this paper consumes. The final statements are: the existence of a projective normal 𝒮^BB over Z_(p) whose generic fibre is the Baily-Borel compactification, stratified flatly by quotients of integral models of Hodge-type Shimura varieties, and of a smooth toroidal 𝒮^tor for an admissible complete smooth cone decomposition, stratified by mixed Shimura varieties with flat boundary divisors, with π: 𝒮^tor → 𝒮^BB extending the identity and compatible with the stratifications, and with the prime-to-p Hecke action extending to both; the explicit complete local ring of 𝒮^BB at a 0-dimensional cusp as the ring of invariants k[[q^λ]]_{λ ≥ 0}^{Δ_K}, with the lattice 𝐁_K ⊂ W(Q), its dual 𝐒_K, the arithmetic group Δ_K and the self-adjoint cone 𝐇, and the action of 𝔹_ℓ = 𝐁_K ⊗ Z[1/ℓ] on it by Σ a_λ q^λ ↦ Σ 𝐞((T,λ))a_λ q^λ; and, over a 1-dimensional cusp, the uniqueness of the cone decomposition, the canonicity of the boundary strata, and the unique extension of the Hecke action to π^{-1} of the complement of the 0-dimensional cusps. Import fans, relative torus embeddings and the rational boundary from ShimuraCompactifications C0-C3, the integral models from the Hodge-type integral-model Part II, and Baily-Borel algebraicity in characteristic zero from ShimuraVarieties V2. This lane owns the boundary; the orthogonal cusp geometry specific to GSpin data, and Chai's cancellation argument on the invariant ideals, are owned elsewhere.
routes.reason: The paper uses Madapusi Pera's integral compactifications as a black box, in exactly the form that PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 already proposed this Part II for. ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans integral compactifications for PEL data only and explicitly disclaims Hodge and abelian type, so nothing in the atlas covers them. The 0-dimensional cusp coordinates go here rather than in the new roadmap because they are a statement about the integral boundary chart, not about Hecke orbits; the argument that uses them, Proposition 8.3, stays with the new roadmap.

routes.title: Supersingular crystals, decay of special endomorphisms and the ordinary Hecke orbit conjecture
routes.brief: Plan the characteristic-p theory that makes Picard ranks of K3 surfaces jump over function fields, and the ordinary Hecke orbit conjecture that follows from it. Work over k = F_p-bar with p ≥ 5, with 𝒮 the canonical integral model of the GSpin Shimura variety of a quadratic Z-lattice (L,Q) of signature (b,2), b ≥ 3, self-dual at p, and with C an irreducible smooth proper curve mapping finitely to 𝒮_k with ordinary generic point and lying in no special divisor. The final theorems are the four results of Maulik, Shankar and Tang. (1) Theorem 1.2: such a C meets ∪_{p ∤ m} Z(m) at infinitely many k-points. (2) Theorem 1.1, its consequence through the Kuga-Satake period map: a generically ordinary non-isotrivial family of K3 surfaces over a proper curve in characteristic p ≥ 5, whose generic Picard lattice has discriminant prime to p, has infinitely many fibres of larger Picard rank. (3) Theorem 1.4: the prime-to-p Hecke orbit of an ordinary point is dense in 𝒮_{F_p}, both in the orthogonal case and in the unitary case of an imaginary quadratic field split at p with an O_K-Hermitian lattice of signature (n,1) of discriminant prime to p; this is the Chai-Oort conjecture for these Shimura varieties. (4) Theorem 5.15, the decay lemma in a general Newton stratum, which is the natural generalisation of the local engine. Cover, in this order. First the local crystalline theory at a supersingular point P of 𝒮_k: the F-crystal 𝕃 = 𝐋_{cris,P}(W) with its σ-linear φ and 𝓛 = 𝕃^{φ=1}; Ogus's orthogonal decomposition of 𝓛, the type t_P and the Artin invariant t_P/2, with superspecial meaning t_P = 2; the induced decomposition of 𝕃; the normal form of 𝓛_0, the classification of the crystals 𝕃_0 by a cyclic vector v, and the resulting cyclic Frobenius matrix B_0; the three cases for 𝓛_1 and the reduction to the split case by embedding. Then Kisin's description of the formal neighbourhood of P together with the F-crystal on it, in coordinates: the Hodge cocharacter, the opposite unipotent, Spf R = O-hat_{𝒮,P} and Frob = u ∘ (φ ⊗ σ); and the equation of the non-ordinary locus, which is y_1 = 0 at a non-superspecial supersingular point and the quadric Q = 0 at a superspecial one. Then the decay lemmas: rapid and very rapid decay of a special endomorphism; the existence of a rapidly decaying saturated rank-2 submodule of 𝓛 at a non-superspecial supersingular point, and the sharper superspecial statement with its two alternatives; their translation into the index bounds |L_1/L_n| ≥ p^{2+2r} and their superspecial refinements; and the generalisation to Newton strata. The proofs need the horizontal section w-tilde = lim Frob^n(w), the infinite product F_∞ = ∏(I + F^{(i)}), de Jong's criterion for lifting over k[t]/t^s through the PD envelopes D_s, the combinatorics of minimal index tuples, and the F_p-linear algebra of the row R-bar_{n+1}. Record explicitly why Grothendieck-Messing theory is too weak in equicharacteristic p, and the formal curve whose local multiplicities grow exponentially, which shows the algebraicity of C cannot be dropped. Then the intersection-theoretic argument: the expected local share g_P(m) = (h_P/(p-1))|q_L(m)|; the successive minima of the L_n and the lower bound a_i(n) ≫ n^{i/b}; truncation; the negligible contribution of non-supersingular points; the splitting of the supersingular contribution into a main term and an error, the uniform error bound, the theta series of the auxiliary lattices L'_n and the comparison of their Eisenstein coefficients with q_L(m), and the conclusion that the supersingular contribution is a fixed fraction α' < 1 of the expected share. Finally the Hecke orbit argument: Chai's cancellation argument at a 0-dimensional cusp, transported to the integral minimal compactification; the analysis at a 1-dimensional cusp, where the fibres are abelian-scheme torsors over a modular curve and ℓ-power Hecke translates fill a fibre; the existence of a generically ordinary proper curve in the closure of a Hecke orbit and the fact that it may be chosen outside every special divisor; the ℓ-adic monodromy lemma; and the induction on b that deduces Theorem 1.4 from Theorem 1.2. Import, and do not rebuild: the GSpin Shimura variety, the Kuga-Satake abelian scheme, the realisations 𝐋_?, special endomorphisms, the special divisors 𝒵(m), the tautological bundle ω with the Hasse invariant, the identity i_P(C.Z(m)) = Σ_n #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m} and the supersingular rank dichotomy from the orthogonal Part II of Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake); the Weil representation ρ_L, the Eisenstein series E_0 with the Bruinier-Kuss coefficients and the Borcherds, Howard-Madapusi Pera modularity of the generating series from the Part II of Gross-Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights); Madapusi Pera's integral minimal and toroidal compactifications of Hodge-type Shimura varieties and the 0-dimensional cusp coordinates from the Part II of Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary); Dieudonné theory from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 and Grothendieck-Messing from R07.6; crystals and F-crystals from CrystallineCohomology CR.1 and CR.3; Serre-Tate theory from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4; successive minima, local densities, theta series and the Siegel mass formula from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1, GN.3 and GN.4; Dirichlet L-functions from AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1; the modular curve and its universal elliptic curve from the Tau Ceti roadmap on modular curves; and Witt vectors, Clifford algebras, the spin group and lattice covolumes from the pinned libraries.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas follows this proof. A search of data/atlas.json finds no layer mentioning the Hecke orbit conjecture, Chai-Oort, Serre-Tate coordinates for Hecke orbits, supersingular K3 crystals, the Artin invariant, or the decay of lattices of special endomorphisms; "hecke orbit", "serre-tate" and "k3 surface" return nothing at all, and the hits for "supersingular" are about elliptic curves, Dieudonné slopes and crystalline descent, not about Ogus's classification of supersingular K3 crystals. Among the pending proposals, OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake owns the integral model and the special divisors, GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights the Arakelov heights of those divisors over number fields, ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary the integral boundary charts, and HeckeOrbitsAndAndréPinkZannier a different subject: generalised Hecke orbits, Galois lower bounds and the André-Pink-Zannier conjecture in characteristic zero, not the Chai-Oort density conjecture in characteristic p. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0 plans Newton strata and central leaves for unitary Shimura varieties in the Caraiani-Scholze programme, which is neither the orthogonal deformation theory nor the decay estimates. This is a new roadmap rather than a Part II because its two endpoints, Theorem 1.1 on Picard ranks of K3 surfaces over function fields and Theorem 1.4 on the ordinary Hecke orbit conjecture, belong to two different existing directions and are joined only by the local crystalline engine this roadmap builds. It is the characteristic-p companion of the lane that PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 opened over number fields: there the local input was Arakelov-theoretic and the global input a height computation, here the local input is Ogus's and Kisin's deformation theory of crystals and the global input is the same Borcherds generating series, so the two share their set-up but not their mathematics.

These four items are general facts about positive definite quadratic lattices that the existing roadmap plans and the paper is a good source for. GN.1 is titled convex-body and successive-minima theorems and is where the successive minima μ_i(n) of a positive definite lattice and the products a_i(n) belong. GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates, which is where Eskin's bound for the number of lattice points of bounded norm in terms of the successive minima belongs; the paper needs it in the form whose implied constant depends only on the rank, so that it applies uniformly to the whole nested family {L_n}, and §7.2 is a clean statement of that need. GN.3 plans reduction domains, local representation densities, mass formulas and theta-series interfaces: the local density δ(ℓ,L,m) with the uniform bound δ(ℓ,L,m) ≍ 1 for rk L ≥ 5, and the Siegel mass formula in the form that gives the Fourier coefficients of the Eisenstein part of the theta series of a lattice, are exactly that. The sibling extraction PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 routed the same material to the same three layers, so this coalesces with it.

AN.1 plans zeta and Dirichlet L-functions. The Kronecker-symbol character χ_D attached to a discriminant D ≡ 0,1 mod 4, and the twisted divisor sums σ_s(m,χ) = Σ_{d|m}χ(d)d^s, are the elementary companions of those L-functions and are used, in §7.3 and in the coefficient formulae of Theorems 7.4 and 7.15, exactly as such. The paper is a good source for them and nothing else in the atlas plans them.

sourceIssues.reason: The displayed series is (2/(1-p^{-2}))(h(p^{-1}+1)/p² + hp/p⁴ + hp²/p⁶ + ···).
